question: A QR code can still scan with a chunk torn away. At most, how much of it can be lost?
answer: Up to about 30%, at the highest of four error correction levels; the others recover about 7%, 15% and 25%. Reed–Solomon codes store extra symbols worked out from the data, so missing parts can be rebuilt. That spare capacity is what lets a logo sit in the middle.
move: Deliberate redundancy is what lets a message survive damage.
ask: Which important thing of mine has no spare copy if part of it is lost?
trap: Almost none, since one missing square seems fatal.
source: Denso Wave, QR code error correction
